title: Safety Accordion: Staged Traffic Scheduler with Multi-Metric Early-Stop
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a new staged traffic scheduler ("Safety Accordion") for canary rollouts that supports fine-grained step schedules, shadow mirroring ramps, A/B splits, and multi-metric early-stop guardrails. The scheduler will expose a declarative policy surface for product and SRE teams (step_percentages, step_duration, hold_conditions, probation_windows) and a runtime evaluator that enforces safety lanes and auto-rollback when guardrails violate. Goal: reduce manual intervention during rollouts while minimizing customer impact and rollout time.
acceptance_criteria: Declarative schedule format v1 accepted by PM and SRE: supports step list with percentage and duration
Runtime enforces at least three concurrent guardrail types: latency SLAs, error-rate spikes, and quality regressions (eval-based)
Auto-rollback triggers within configured probation_window and provides telemetry + reason for rollback
Shadow traffic mirroring can be configured per-route with adjustable sample rate and delayed promotion
E2E tests demonstrating staged rollout to 1%, 5%, 20%, 50% with successful early-stop at 5% for injected latency failures
Console UI surface renders accordion view of scheduled steps and shows active safety lane state
technical_notes: Scheduler model: deterministic step engine with time and metric-based transitions. Steps defined as [{pct, min_duration, hold_condition}]

Hold_conditions implemented as boolean expressions over aggregated metrics (p99_latency > X OR error_rate > Y OR eval_regression > Z). We'll compile expressions into a lightweight evaluator (Lua-like sandbox or precompiled WASM) to avoid heavy eval costs
Traffic ramp strategy: exponential vs linear profiles supported. Default profile uses small first steps (1% -> 5% -> 20%) to limit blast radius
Probation windows: metric smoothing with EWMA (alpha=0.3) and minimum sample requirements to avoid noisy decisions
Early-stop algorithm: combine threshold checks with a Bayesian posterior probability test to avoid false positives during low volume

Shadow mirroring: mirror path runs off-path in read-only mode and collects quality metrics; support delayed promotion where mirrored results are compared to production for N minutes before being allowed into canary
Rollback: policy attaches rollback_action (immediate|staged-revert|pause) and generates a rollback runbook with telemetry links
Telemetry: expose per-step traces, evidence for guardrail triggers, and token-level latency breakdowns for reproducibility
API design: PATCH /rollouts/{id}/schedule to update, POST /rollouts to create declarative policy, GET /rollouts/{id}/state for active runtime state
Authorization: RBAC enforced; only rollout owners or SRE group can bypass safety lanes
rollback_policy: Default: immediate rollback to previous stable variant if any guardrail breaches occur in two consecutive polling windows within the probation_window. Configurable modes: immediate, staged-revert (roll back in reverse steps), or pause-and-alert. All rollback events must produce a deterministic diff + reason in the console and trigger incident webhook.
decisions: Use EWMA + Bayesian check for early-stop rather than raw thresholds to reduce false positives at low volume
Sandboxed evaluator chosen as WASM to allow future user-provided guard expressions safely
Default schedules will bias toward conservative small first steps to align with enterprise SLAs
Shadow mirroring will be opt-in per-route to avoid doubling cost on high-QPS endpoints
